sector: Consumer Staples / Meal Kits & Online Grocery
overview: My Food Bag Group is a New Zealand-founded meal-kit and online food-solutions company that delivers pre-portioned recipe boxes and, increasingly, ready-made meals and one-off gifting products direct to households nationwide. It operates a multi-brand portfolio (My Food Bag, Bargain Box, Fresh Start) targeting different price points and dietary needs, supplemented by the newer My Food Bag Shop, a subscription-free retail channel. The company is single-country (New Zealand only), dual-listed on the NZX and ASX, and as of April 2026 is subject to a live board-initiated strategic review of its ownership and capital structure.

business_model.summary: MFB sells weekly (and one-off) recipe boxes and ready-made meals via a semi-subscription model: customers select a plan/brand and order cadence but can pause or skip weeks at will, so revenue is transactional/renewal-based rather than contractually recurring. Revenue is effectively Active Customers x average meal-kit order frequency x average order value, plus a growing non-kit Shop/Ready-Made contribution. Gross margin (~49%) reflects ingredient cost of goods; contribution margin after variable delivery/labour costs runs ~21%. FY26: revenue NZ$170.2m (+5.0%), Active Customers 57,100 (FY25: 57,000), average meal frequency 5.5 orders/customer (FY25: 5.4), average order value NZ$133.71 (FY25: $130.06).

revenue_streams.name: Fresh Start (weight-loss/wellness meal kits, incl. GLP-1 support menu)
My Food Bag Shop (Ready Made meals, gifting, no-subscription one-offs)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - new channel, first full year FY26

business_model.customer_type: B2C household subscribers (predominantly), with an emerging B2B/corporate gifting segment via the Shop
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand (Auckland and Christchurch fulfilment/distribution facilities); no meaningful international revenue

main_competitors: Uber Eats / My Food Bag Shop-style convenience delivery
generic supermarket grocery (the true largest competitor for share of wallet)
competitive_position.market_position: Self-described 'clear market leader in the meal kit category' in New Zealand, but the category itself is a small, low-growth niche within total grocery spend, and its historical active-customer base has shrunk by more than 20% from post-COVID peaks (~72k in 2021 versus 57.1k in FY26)

moat_factors.description: Strong New Zealand brand awareness (10+ years operating, ambassador Nadia Lim, Canstar Blue 'Best Rated Meal Kit' 2025), sourcing >98% of fresh proteins/produce domestically, which resonates with Kiwi consumers versus a global entrant like HelloFresh
My Food Bag/Bargain Box/Fresh Start let the company capture value-, mainstream- and health-focused segments simultaneously, cushioning against a single competitor undercutting on price
Two established fulfilment centres, new integrated warehouse/inventory system (Auckland Feb-2026, Christchurch Mar-2026), Pick-to-Light technology improving pick accuracy and cost
Virtually none - customers can pause, skip, or switch to a rival meal kit or simply go back to supermarket shopping with no penalty; this is the core weakness of the category economically
No network effects; a two-sided or platform moat does not exist in this business

weaknesses: No structural switching costs - meal kits are a discretionary, easily substitutable purchase and churn is structurally high across the category
Small scale versus HelloFresh, a global player now reaching ~84% of the NZ population (up from ~72% a year earlier) with far greater purchasing/marketing scale
Active customer base nearly halved from IPO-era highs and has only stabilised, not meaningfully grown, over the past three years
Single country, single consumer segment concentration - no geographic diversification to offset a NZ-specific downturn
Thin free float and illiquid stock (~NZ$70m market cap at $0.29) limits institutional interest absent a takeout
Vulnerable to supermarket duopoly (Woolworths NZ, Foodstuffs) replicating simplified meal-kit/ready-meal offers with far greater store/logistics reach and pricing power

growth_drivers: Retention and lifetime-value improvements: average meal frequency rose to 5.5/customer (from 5.4) and management cites improving tenure/retention as a key FY26 driver

My Food Bag Shop expansion - subscription-free Ready Made meals, gifting, care packages, same-day delivery; first full year of operation in FY26, now expanding into new categories (fresh cakes, flowers) and reaching new corporate/gifting occasions

Health/dietary product line extension - Diabetes Plan (launched Apr-2025), GLP-1 weight-loss-medication support menu (launched Jun-2025/2026), Gluten Free Bag growth, Fresh Start's 8-week Reset programme
Larger-household and customisation SKUs - Serves 6 option (early 2025) and 'Double Protein' customisation (early 2026) driving average order value up to $133.71

Operational efficiency/cost discipline - Pick-to-Light, Dynamic Box and Ice packaging optimisation, new warehouse management system, AI-driven productivity - supporting margin even as input costs rise

Balance sheet repair enabling capital returns - net debt cut from $6.9m to $1.9m in FY26, FY26 total dividend 1.90 cps fully imputed (10.1% trailing yield at $0.26), dividend reinvestment plan in operation
M&A/take-private optionality - live strategic review with Cameron Partners could crystallise a premium to the current depressed share price if a transaction eventuates

business.description: Meal kits inherently have high customer turnover; active customers of 57.1k in FY26 remain well below the ~70k+ levels seen in 2021-22, and growth has been essentially flat for three years despite marketing investment
HelloFresh NZ now reaches ~84% of the NZ population (up from ~72%) with global-scale purchasing and marketing budgets that MFB, as a single-market operator, cannot match

Woolworths NZ and Foodstuffs (New World, Pak'nSave) can offer their own meal-solution/ready-meal ranges bundled into a weekly grocery shop, competing for the same wallet share with far greater reach and lower incremental cost
Revenue base of ~NZ$170m makes MFB a minor player against multi-billion-dollar grocery and international meal-kit competitors; no product diversification beyond food-at-home solutions
Nadia Lim's personal brand is deeply woven into marketing across all MFB brands; loss of the relationship would be a marketing setback

financial.description: Net debt reduced to $1.9m at FY26 year-end, a genuine positive, but the business still operates with limited scale and a working-capital-sensitive model
Market cap of only ~NZ$70m at $0.29 and limited daily trading volume mean the stock can be volatile on small news flow and difficult for larger holders to enter/exit

regulatory.risk: Food safety and product recall exposure
regulatory.description: As a fresh-food logistics business, any contamination, mislabelling, or recall event carries reputational and financial risk
No unusual regulatory overhang identified beyond standard NZ food-safety, advertising and consumer-protection law

macro.description: Meal kits are a discretionary spend that competes directly with cheaper 'cook it yourself' grocery shopping; management repeatedly flags 'challenging economic conditions' and food-price inflation (4.1% in the year to Sep-2025) compressing gross margin
100% exposure to the New Zealand economy/consumer - no diversification if NZ growth, employment or consumer confidence deteriorates further
H1 FY26 gross margin fell to 48.5% (from 49.8%) on food price inflation; FY26 full-year gross margin also slipped slightly to 49.0% (FY25: 49.3%) before recovering somewhat in H2

execution.risk: Strategic review concludes with no transaction
execution.description: The Board has explicitly stated 'there is no certainty that any transaction will eventuate' and remaining NZX-listed is one of the options on the table; if the review concludes without a deal, any speculative premium in the share price could unwind

Chair Tony Carter retires effective the 19-Nov-2026 half-year results, to be succeeded by independent director Mark Powell (subject to re-election at the 19-Aug-2026 ASM) - a routine but notable governance change occurring alongside the live strategic review

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The NZ online food/meal-kit category remains small relative to total grocery spend and structurally challenged by high churn; management frames the addressable opportunity more broadly as the 'growing online food market' (meal kits plus ready-made meals plus online grocery convenience) rather than meal kits alone, which is itself a signal that pure meal-kit growth has matured
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical/discretionary - demand is sensitive to household budgets and cost-of-living pressure; management has explicitly called out 'challenging economic conditions' and 'inflationary environment' as a persistent headwind through FY25 and FY26
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (modest debt now, net debt just $1.9m at FY26 year-end) but moderate indirect sensitivity via NZ consumer discretionary spending and mortgage-rate-driven household budgets
key_input_costs: Fresh produce and protein ingredient costs (>98% NZ-sourced)

recent_developments.event: Chair succession announced: Tony Carter to retire as Chair effective the 19-Nov-2026 half-year results date; independent director Mark Powell to become Chair, subject to re-election at the 19-Aug-2026 ASM

FY26 annual results (year to 31-Mar-2026): revenue NZ$170.2m (+5.0%), EBITDA $16.4m (FY25: $16.1m), NPAT $6.7m (+5.3%), net debt cut to $1.9m (from $6.9m), free cash flow $8.5m, Active Customers 57.1k, final dividend 1.15 cps fully imputed (total FY26 dividend 1.90 cps, ~10.1% trailing yield at $0.26); stock reportedly surged ~7.5% on the release

Board announced a price-sensitive strategic review of ownership, capital structure and strategic options, appointing Cameron Partners Limited as financial adviser; explicitly no certainty a transaction will occur and continued NZX listing remains an option; shares reportedly jumped as much as ~17% in the week of the announcement, MFB's best week in nearly a year

H1 FY26 interim results (six months to 30-Sep-2025): revenue $85.4m (+3.8%), EBITDA $7.2m, NPAT $2.9m broadly flat, Active Customers 61,300 (up from 60,100 in H1 FY25), gross margin fell to 48.5% (from 49.8%) on 4.1% food price inflation, net debt reduced to $5.5m, interim dividend of 0.75 cps declared with a DRP at no discount

Product/brand initiatives: launch of Diabetes Plan with Diabetes NZ (Apr-2025), GLP-1 weight-loss-medication support menu (mid-2025/2026), 'Double Protein' customisation across all three brands (early 2026), continued Nadia Lim brand campaigns ('Dinner with Nadia', Auckland FC partnership)

New integrated warehouse and inventory management system went live at Auckland (Feb-2026) and Christchurch (Mar-2026) facilities, improving stock visibility and batch traceability and providing a scalable supply-chain platform

guidance.as_of: FY26 Annual Results / Outlook commentary, 21-May-2026 (with prior signal from H1 FY26 interim, Nov-2025)

items.metric: Full-year profitability (H1 FY26 guidance, since superseded by FY26 actuals)
items.target: broadly in line with prior year
items.notes: At the H1 FY26 interim (Nov-2025) management guided FY26 profitability to be 'broadly in line with the prior year'; actual FY26 NPAT of $6.7m came in +5.3% above FY25's $6.3m, a modest beat

Management stated 'early trading in FY27 has remained encouraging, with demand trends continuing to track positively' and that the operating environment 'is expected to remain challenging in the near term, with ongoing cost pressures across the supply chain'; no specific revenue/EBITDA range provided for FY27

Board states the review 'remains in its preliminary stages' as of the FY26 annual report (20-May-2026) and there is 'no certainty that any transaction involving My Food Bag will eventuate'; company committed to continuous disclosure updates

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Tony Carter and CEO Mark Winter reiterated that FY26 strategic objectives (growing meal-kit leadership, expanding into the wider online food category via flexibility, convenience and value) remain unchanged into FY27. Management flagged continued cost pressure and food-price inflation as the primary near-term headwind, offset by disciplined cost control and 'a measured approach to pricing' intended to preserve a consistent weekly price point for customers. No formal quantitative FY27 revenue/EBITDA/NPAT guidance range has been issued; commentary is directional/qualitative only, alongside acknowledgement that the ownership/strategic review outcome is unresolved.

bull_case: Turnaround now visible in the numbers: five consecutive years of stabilising-to-growing revenue, EBITDA and NPAT after the 2021-23 IPO-era collapse, alongside near-elimination of net debt ($1.9m at FY26 year-end) and restored dividends (1.90 cps FY26, ~10% trailing yield)

Live strategic review with Cameron Partners creates genuine, market-acknowledged takeover/re-rating optionality on a stock the Board itself says is undervalued relative to recent operating performance; the ~17% share-price jump on the review announcement shows the market assigns real probability to a value-unlocking outcome

Diversification beyond core meal kits into My Food Bag Shop (ready-made meals, gifting, same-day delivery) and health-focused product lines (GLP-1 support, Diabetes Plan, Fresh Start) expands the addressable market beyond the maturing weeknight meal-kit category

Improving unit economics - average meal frequency and order value both rising, customer compensation/complaints falling, NPS at record highs (70% for Christmas) - suggest genuine retention/loyalty gains rather than just price increases

Very depressed valuation relative to history: shares trade around $0.26-0.29 versus an $1.85 IPO price (roughly 84% below issue), so even a modest re-rating or a moderate takeover premium would be a large percentage return from current levels
bear_case: Meal kits are a structurally low-moat, high-churn category with no real switching costs; MFB's active customer base remains roughly 20-25% below its 2021 peak years after the IPO, and growth since has been essentially flat to marginal despite continuous marketing/product investment

HelloFresh, a global-scale competitor, now covers ~84% of the NZ population (versus ~72% a year prior) and can out-market and out-discount a single-country operator like MFB indefinitely; the supermarket duopoly (Woolworths NZ, Foodstuffs) is a further structural threat that can bundle meal solutions into everyday grocery shops

The strategic review may simply conclude with 'no transaction' - management has explicitly flagged this outcome as possible - in which case any speculative M&A premium currently in the share price could reverse, leaving the stock to trade on its standalone (much lower historical) fundamentals

Small, single-country, single-category business (~NZ$170m revenue) with thin free float and low liquidity, making it a poor fit for larger institutional capital and vulnerable to outsized moves on limited news flow

Margins remain under persistent pressure from food-price inflation (gross margin dipped to 48.5% in H1 FY26 before partially recovering) and management itself continues to characterise the operating environment as 'challenging' with 'ongoing cost pressures' expected to persist into FY27
